sections.title: Kera-Disk Technology and Safety Circuits
body: The plate's material choice and the safety system are engineered to solve two distinct problems: heating fast without damaging the surface, and protecting the user and sample without slowing anyone down.

The Kera-Disk plate uses aluminium specifically for its heat transfer speed, then adds a wafer-thin ceramic coating on top for chemical and scratch resistance, which is what allows the 35% faster heat-up without sacrificing durability. On the safety side, two independent circuits handle two separate failure modes: one shuts off heating if the set temperature is overshot by 25°C, and a completely separate one shuts off heating if the Pt1000 sensor isn't actually immersed in the liquid, since a dry sensor would otherwise let the plate keep heating well past a safe point.

sections.eyebrow: Performance Testing: Findenser vs Air and Water Condensers
sections.title: Performance Testing: Findenser vs Air and Water Condensers
body: The test conditions were consistent and specific: 500 mL of solvent in a 1,000 mL flask, run for 16 hours, heated 10°C above each solvent's boiling point.

Against a standard air condenser, the difference was stark with low boiling point solvents. Acetone and DCM boiled completely dry using the air condenser, while Findenser retained 95% of the solvent under identical conditions. With medium boiling point solvents, Findenser still showed improved retention, particularly at larger volumes and higher temperatures. Against a water condenser, retention matched within experimental error across the range tested, with diethyl ether the one confirmed exception where Findenser isn't recommended.

sections.eyebrow: Water Cost and Return on Investment
sections.title: Water Cost and Return on Investment
body: Running water for a condenser has a real, ongoing cost, even though it's easy to overlook once the tap is running.

Based on a single UK tap at 2.5 litres per minute, a water condenser running just 4 hours a day consumes 600 litres daily, working out to roughly £533 a year on that region's water tariff. Running 24 hours a day, that figure rises to over £3,000 annually, for one condenser. Against that basis, Findenser is stated to pay for itself in under 6 months. These are UK reference figures specifically; actual water and disposal costs in India will differ, but the underlying principle, that running water for reflux cooling carries a real recurring cost, applies regardless of region.
Product expert note: Tell our team how many condensers you're currently running on tap water and for how long each day, and Inkarp will help estimate the potential savings for your setup.

faqs.question: What is the Heat-On Block System used for?
faqs.answer: It replaces oil baths and heating mantles for heating round-bottom flasks from 10 mL to 5 L, offering faster, safer, and more energy-efficient heating.

faqs.question: What is the StarFish Work Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a modular heating and stirring system for synthesis, distillation, and extraction, running individual or parallel vessels on your existing hotplate.

faqs.question: What's the difference between MonoBlocks and PolyBlocks?
faqs.answer: MonoBlocks hold multiple wells of the same size for uniform parallel runs; PolyBlocks use small mixable segments to accommodate any combination of vessel sizes.

faqs.question: Can I use the gas or water manifold without the rest of StarFish?
faqs.answer: Yes, both manifolds are designed to work independently of the StarFish blocks and clamps.

faqs.question: How do I set up multiple condensers with one water source?
faqs.answer: Use the Water Manifold, which distributes coolant from a single source to up to 5 condensers and recombines it to one outlet pipe, using two manifolds per set-up.

faqs.question: How does the clamp actually hold glassware in place?
faqs.answer: The lower clamp's rubber strap grips the flask neck for lifting, while the upper clamp's Velcro strap lets a condenser slide through it while still being safely restrained.

faqs.question: Can I use glassware I already own with StarFish?
faqs.answer: Yes, StarFish accommodates glassware from Carousel 12 Plus, Carousel 6 Plus, and GreenHouse directly, alongside standard laboratory glassware.

faqs.question: What hotplate does StarFish work with?
faqs.answer: All leading stirring hotplate brands, with base plates available for round or square top plates.

faqs.question: How hot can the blocks go?
faqs.answer: Up to 260°C, using chemical-resistant anodised aluminium construction.

faqs.question: What is the price of the StarFish Work Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your block type, manifold, and clamp configuration. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the StarFish Work Station in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the Radleys StarFish Work Station in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

longForm.heroLead: Keep your own hotplate. Mix blocks, clamps, and manifolds to fit the experiment. Buying a dedicated setup for every reaction type adds up fast, in cost and in bench space. StarFish is built to replace that with one modular system on the hotplate you already own. Choose MonoBlocks when every vessel is the same size, or PolyBlocks when they're not, mixing segments to fit any combination up to 500 mL. Add a gas/vacuum manifold or a water manifold, each distributing to up to five positions, and either works completely independently of StarFish too. It fits all leading hotplate brands, round or square, and accepts glassware from your existing Carousel 12 Plus, Carousel 6 Plus, or GreenHouse systems directly. Spare components store in a drawer, not across your bench.

sections.title: MonoBlocks, PolyBlocks and Reducing Inserts
body: The block choice is the first real decision, and it comes down to whether your vessels are all one size or genuinely mixed.

MonoBlocks hold multiple wells of the same size, built for running several identical vessels in parallel. PolyBlocks take the opposite approach: small segments that mix and match to accommodate any combination of vessel, up to 5 segments per StarFish. Both share the same core construction, anodised aluminium rated to 260°C, both stackable to save space, both individually labelled, and both accept the same reducing inserts down to 5 mL.
